topic: Entergy's $1 billion Traceview power plant: the Oct. 13 Permit Board vote and what comes after it
angle: A vote before it happens. The state Permit Board meets Tuesday, Oct. 13 at 9 a.m. at MDEQ's Jackson office on the air permit for the 754-megawatt plant. If the board has voted, report what it decided and the gates still ahead: the water pretreatment permit (MSP092492), the local zoning approvals the permit leaves to Entergy, and the 18-month construction clock in Condition 1.19. If it has not met yet, write only if MDEQ has posted the agenda at mdeq.ms.gov or filed something new since the Wire's Oct. 6 story.

topic: Jackson's new per-ton landfill fees: the council vote and what a household pays
angle: Money out of readers' pockets. The Pipeline expects the council to take up the fee ordinance for adoption at a regular meeting in October: Section 106-148 of the city code, $10 a ton for residents and $20 a ton for commercial haulers and anyone from outside the city, replacing $5 per cubic yard. Start with the council agenda and minutes at jacksonms.gov, because the Wire's own stories differ on whether the Oct. 6 item was an introduction or a vote. Report what the council did, whether the city has published the tonnage and cost study behind the rates, and whether the Byram site has reopened. The Wire's Sept. 25 story already has the per-ton arithmetic, so add only what is new.

topic: Jackson's Nov. 3 tourism tax vote, explained: what the two increases cost and where the money goes
angle: A plain explainer on the ballot question. Jackson voters decide on Nov. 3 whether to raise the prepared-food tax by 0.5% (from 1% to 1.5%) and the lodging tax by 1% (from 1% to 2%), with the money dedicated to Visit Jackson, the first change since 1983. The Wire's Aug. 27 story has the rates and the 60% threshold; its Sept. 25 story said the council resolution and the certified ballot language had not been published in the county's meeting record. Find them and S.B. 3328, then say in plain words what the ballot asks, who collects and who spends the money, and what a yes or no vote changes.
